## Motivation

The foundation of [[stochastic-calculus]] is integration with respect to
**diffusions**, a class of continuous-time [[markov-process|Markov processes]]
with almost surely continuous sample paths (see [[ito-diffusion]]). Several
constructions exist, notably those of **Itô** and **Stratonovich**. They
differ in where the integrand is evaluated on each small interval: the Itô
integral uses the left endpoint, which keeps the integral a martingale and is
the convention in finance. Brownian paths have infinite variation, so the
integral cannot be defined pathwise as a Riemann-Stieltjes integral, which is
why a separate construction is needed.

Let $B$ be a (one-dimensional) [[brownian-motion|Brownian motion]] on a
filtered probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},(\mathcal{F}_t),\mathbb{P})$
(see [[filtrations-and-adapted-processes]]). A diffusion has the form

$$
X_{t+s}-X_t=\int_t^{t+s}\mu(X_u,u)\,du+\int_t^{t+s}\sigma(X_u,u)\,dB_u,
$$

and the second term is an Itô integral of the process $\sigma(X_u,u)$.

## The Class of Integrands

:::{.definition data-title="The Class $\mathcal{V}(S,T)$"}

$\mathcal{V}=\mathcal{V}(S,T)$ is the class of functions
$f(t,\omega):[0,\infty)\times\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$ such that

1. $(t,\omega)\mapsto f(t,\omega)$ is $\mathcal{B}\times\mathcal{F}$-measurable,
   where $\mathcal{B}$ is the Borel $\sigma$-algebra on $[0,\infty)$,
2. $f(t,\cdot)$ is $\mathcal{F}_t$-adapted, and
3. $\mathbb{E}\left[\int_S^Tf(t,\omega)^2\,dt\right]<\infty$.

:::

The aim is to define

$$
\mathcal{I}[f](\omega)=\int_S^Tf(t,\omega)\,dB_t(\omega),\qquad f\in\mathcal{V}.
$$

We first define it for step functions and then extend by approximation.

## Elementary Functions

:::{.definition data-title="Elementary Function"}

A function $\phi\in\mathcal{V}$ is **elementary** if

$$
\phi(t,\omega)=\sum_je_j(\omega)\,\mathbb{1}_{[t_j,t_{j+1})}(t).
$$

:::

Since $\phi\in\mathcal{V}$, each $e_j$ must be $\mathcal{F}_{t_j}$-measurable.
For such $\phi$ define

$$
\int_S^T\phi(t,\omega)\,dB_t(\omega)=\sum_{j\ge 0}e_j(\omega)
\left[B_{t_{j+1}}-B_{t_j}\right](\omega).
$$

:::{.theorem data-title="Itô Isometry for Elementary Functions"}

If $\phi$ is bounded and elementary, then

$$
\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\int_S^T\phi\,dB_t\right)^2\right]
=\mathbb{E}\left[\int_S^T\phi^2\,dt\right].
$$

:::

:::{.proof}

Write $\Delta B_j=B_{t_{j+1}}-B_{t_j}$. By the independent increments of
Brownian motion, and since $e_i,e_j$ are measurable with respect to the past,

$$
\mathbb{E}[e_ie_j\Delta B_i\Delta B_j]=
\begin{cases}
0 & i\neq j,\\
\mathbb{E}[e_j^2]\,(t_{j+1}-t_j) & i=j.
\end{cases}
$$

Hence

$$
\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\int_S^T\phi\,dB\right)^2\right]
=\sum_{i,j}\mathbb{E}[e_ie_j\Delta B_i\Delta B_j]
=\sum_j\mathbb{E}[e_j^2](t_{j+1}-t_j)
=\mathbb{E}\left[\int_S^T\phi^2\,dt\right].
$$

:::

## Extension to $\mathcal{V}$

The extension takes three steps, each showing that a larger class can be
approximated in $L^2(\mathbb{P}\times dt)$ by a smaller one.

**Step 1.** Let $g\in\mathcal{V}$ be bounded with $g(\cdot,\omega)$ continuous
for each $\omega$. Then there are elementary $\phi_n\in\mathcal{V}$ with

$$
\mathbb{E}\left[\int_S^T(g-\phi_n)^2\,dt\right]\to 0.
$$

:::{.proof}

Take $\phi_n=\sum_jg(t_j,\omega)\mathbb{1}_{[t_j,t_{j+1})}$ on a partition with
mesh tending to $0$. It is elementary since $g$ is adapted, and by continuity
of $g(\cdot,\omega)$ we have $\int_S^T(g-\phi_n)^2dt\to 0$ for each $\omega$.
The claim follows by bounded convergence.

:::

**Step 2.** Let $h\in\mathcal{V}$ be bounded. Then there are bounded
$g_n\in\mathcal{V}$, continuous in $t$ for each $\omega$, with
$\mathbb{E}\left[\int_S^T(h-g_n)^2dt\right]\to 0$.

:::{.proof}

Let $\psi_n$ be a non-negative continuous function supported in $[-1/n,0]$
with $\int\psi_n=1$, and set
$g_n(t,\omega)=\int_0^t\psi_n(s-t)h(s,\omega)\,ds$. Then $g_n$ is continuous
in $t$, bounded, and adapted since it only uses values of $h$ up to time $t$.
For each $\omega$, $\int_S^T(g_n-h)^2dt\to 0$ because $\psi_n$ is an
approximate identity, and bounded convergence gives the result.

:::

**Step 3.** Let $f\in\mathcal{V}$. Then there are bounded $h_n\in\mathcal{V}$
with $\mathbb{E}\left[\int_S^T(f-h_n)^2dt\right]\to 0$.

:::{.proof}

Truncate, $h_n=\max(-n,\min(f,n))$. Then $|f-h_n|\le|f|$, so dominated
convergence applies since $\mathbb{E}\int f^2<\infty$.

:::

Combining the steps, every $f\in\mathcal{V}$ admits elementary $\phi_n$ with
$\mathbb{E}\left[\int_S^T(f-\phi_n)^2dt\right]\to 0$.

:::{.definition data-title="Itô Integral"}

For $f\in\mathcal{V}(S,T)$ the **Itô integral** is

$$
\int_S^Tf\,dB_t=\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_S^T\phi_n\,dB_t\quad\text{in }
L^2(\mathbb{P}),
$$

for any sequence of elementary $\phi_n$ with
$\mathbb{E}\left[\int_S^T(f-\phi_n)^2dt\right]\to 0$.

:::

The limit exists because, by the isometry applied to $\phi_n-\phi_m$, the
sequence $\int\phi_n\,dB$ is Cauchy in $L^2(\mathbb{P})$, and it does not
depend on the chosen sequence for the same reason.

## Itô Isometry

The isometry passes to the limit, which gives the main result for Itô
integrals.

:::{.theorem data-title="Itô Isometry"}

For all $f\in\mathcal{V}(S,T)$,

$$
\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\int_S^Tf(t,\omega)\,dB_t\right)^2\right]
=\mathbb{E}\left[\int_S^Tf^2(t,\omega)\,dt\right].
$$

:::

## Properties

:::{.proposition data-title="Properties of the Itô Integral"}

Let $f,g\in\mathcal{V}(0,T)$ and $0\le S<U<T$. Then

1. $\int_S^TfdB_t=\int_S^UfdB_t+\int_U^TfdB_t$ almost surely,
2. $\int_S^T(cf+g)\,dB_t=c\int_S^TfdB_t+\int_S^TgdB_t$ almost surely, for
   constant $c$,
3. $\mathbb{E}\left[\int_S^TfdB_t\right]=0$,
4. $\int_S^TfdB_t$ is $\mathcal{F}_T$-measurable.

:::

These hold for elementary functions by direct computation and extend by
$L^2$-limits. The integral process $t\mapsto\int_0^tf\,dB$ is moreover a
[[martingale-theory|martingale]], and its differential rules are given by the
[[ito-formula]].
